bundle.name: NEXUS Wave 3D closure - v4 bundle
bundle.exit_code_semantics: 0 == every leg reproduced the declared numbers; any other code == the bundle is stale
bundle.provenance_note: Wave 3D v1-v3 bundles are LOST (no bytes present anywhere in the workspace). This bundle is a functional reconstruction: it reproduces every claim from the exact upstream trees, but its artifact hashes are NOT the previously reported ones (see lost_artifacts).

runtime.note: reproduce.sh builds its own venv per leg; the A/B legs install langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.1.2 vs 3.1.1 into separate venvs.

patch_a_async_session.compat_note: composes with Patch B on the #198 tree (leg 10) in full: `bot/handlers.py` applies with an offset, `features/onboarding.py` cleanly. Earlier 'patch does not apply' reports were caused by a stale work directory being reused (the clone helper keeps an existing directory), not by a tree difference; reproduce.sh now removes the work directory before it starts.

patch_b_tests.regenerated_reason: the first revision of the module built the feature-engine container before the chdir/tmp-database setup, so it only passed inside the development clone (which carries a repository-relative data/ directory); the shipped revision chdirs into tmp_path first and creates the ambient tables after the container import.

dispatch_async_session_repair.content_note: exactly the six `bot/handlers.py` hunks of patch_a_async_session.patch, extracted for the #198 dispatch path; no other change

legs.title: Patch B + Patch A composed on the exact PR #198 tree
legs.command: privacy module alone on the base (27 tests) -> apply patch_b_prompt_placement -> rerun -> apply the bot/handlers.py half of Patch A -> run the privacy module plus its six sibling suites (82 tests)
legs.expected: base: 5 failed, 22 passed; patch B only: 3 failed, 24 passed; composed: 1 failed, 81 passed where the single failure is the documented /forget_me transcript-erasure finding

legs.title: dispatch ordering: Patch B, then the dispatch-scoped session repair
legs.command: run tests/unit/test_registered_dispatch.py on the base; apply patch_b_prompt_placement and rerun; apply dispatch_async_session_repair and rerun
legs.expected: base: 2 failed, 4 passed; after Patch B: unchanged 2 failed, 4 passed (Patch B does not repair the boundary); after the dispatch repair: 6 passed

ab_verdict.pin_recommendation: keep 3.1.1; do not change the pin without contrary controlled evidence

patch_a.defect: the async session factories and the injected get_session yield a plain SQLAlchemy AsyncSession (no .exec), while bot/handlers.py called session.exec at 6 sites and features/onboarding.py at 1 -> every free-text message died in _upsert_user before the graph ran

patch_b.defect: _chat_agent interpolated long-term memory into the system prompt, giving stored (attacker-influenceable) text instruction authority; the repair moves it into the user-data position inside [UNTRUSTED STORED MEMORY] ... [END UNTRUSTED STORED MEMORY]

dispatch_ordering.base: 2 failed, 4 passed — both direct dispatch tests die in _upsert_user with AttributeError: 'AsyncSession' object has no attribute 'exec' (bot/handlers.py:130)
dispatch_ordering.patch_b_only: 2 failed, 4 passed — Patch B changes the prompt the graph builds, not the session boundary
dispatch_ordering.reverse_order_tested: dispatch repair then Patch B also gives 6 passed (the two patches touch disjoint files), so there is no order hazard; the dependency is that the dispatch repair is required
dispatch_ordering.structural_property: exactly one MessageHandler(filters.TEXT & ~filters.COMMAND, on_message) is registered and it sits after every CommandHandler, so commands are not swallowed

limitations: PostgreSQL checkpointing is DEFERRED: no postgres service was available, so the #211 A/B covers the SQLite checkpointer only; the acceptance plan is reproducible but unexecuted.
The A/B, checker v3, T-ISO-01 and Patch A/B results are local runs on exact upstream trees; they are not remote CI and not production verification.
No artifact in this bundle has been published to a durable external location; durability today == this workspace path plus the sha256 values recorded here.
The '44-test suite' mentioned in the originating report has no identified composition in the repository and is therefore not claimed.
The dispatch and privacy legs were verified against PR #198's head only; a future head change invalidates them (re-run reproduce.sh).
harness_notes: reproduce.sh removes its work directory before starting; reusing a dirty work directory produces spurious 'patch does not apply' failures.

The privacy and dispatch modules chdir into a temporary directory and create the CWD-relative ambient database *after* the feature-engine container has imported its model modules; without that order the force-join gate reads a table that does not exist yet.

Every patch in patches/ was checked with `git apply --check` against the main, #198, #210 and #211 trees; all apply everywhere, and each leg still applies its patch to the declared base (apply-everywhere means context-compatible, not validated-on).

Each reproduce.sh run truncates its evidence/reproduce_leg*.txt files, so those logs always describe the run that produced them; the curated step logs (evidence/step3_*.log, patch_*.log, dispatch_ordering_*.log, step16_*.log) are written by the individual validation steps.

publication.verification: each commit was re-cloned from https://github.com/bot523h/nexus-ai-agent.git and every file compared by sha256: 45/45, 47/47 and 48/48 identical, zero mismatches
publication.durability_limitation: a git branch is mutable and there is no independent archive or tag; this is recoverable publication, not immutable storage
